facts.population: RPD metal frameworks (30 studies; 815 frameworks or part specimens, mostly in vitro)
facts.intervention: 3D-printed RPD metal frameworks via SLS, SLM or DMLS
facts.comparison: Conventional casting and partial digital methods (CAD/CAM resin pattern followed by casting)
facts.main_result: 3D-printed RPD metal frameworks showed accuracy and mechanical-physical performance comparable or superior to conventional and partially digital methods.
facts.funding_coi: No funding; no competing interests declared
facts.limitations: Evidence limited by methodological variability, moderate risk of bias in many studies, and inconsistencies across designs and parameters.
facts.key_finding: Across 30 mostly in-vitro studies, 3D-printed (SLM/SLS/DMLS) metal RPD frameworks matched or exceeded casting and partially digital frameworks in fit, mechanical and physical properties. The few clinical studies reported improved retention and patient satisfaction.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Printed metal RPD frameworks appear a viable alternative to casting, though evidence is mostly laboratory-based and heterogeneous.

facts.population: 24 participants aged 50-65 with mandibular Kennedy class I partially edentulous arches
facts.intervention: Fully-digital workflow (intraoral scan) for SLM Co-Cr RPD frameworks
facts.comparison: Combined analog-digital workflow (physical impression, stone cast, lab scanner)
outcomes: gap at rest, proximal plate, lingual plate, I-bar clasp terminal
facts.main_result: Overall mean gap was 0.112 mm for combined vs 0.101 mm for fully-digital workflow (P=0.0125); fully-digital was superior in all areas.
facts.key_finding: Fully-digital intraoral-scan workflow gave Co-Cr SLM RPD frameworks with smaller gaps than the analog-digital workflow (0.101 vs 0.112 mm overall), though both were clinically acceptable.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Intraoral scanning can be used for SLM RPD frameworks with equal or slightly better fit than conventional impressions.
